pr_title: *: fix bug of profiling conflict between TopSQL and pprof profile HTTP API
pr_body:
<!--

PR Title Format:

2. *: what's changed

-->

### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close #30890

Problem Summary: Continuous Profiling do cpu profile maybe conflict with TopSQL.

### What is changed and how it works?

This PR introduce a `ParallelCPUProfiler` to be responsible for handling profiling requests. Then both the TopSQL and pprof Profile HTTP API get profile data by `ParallelCPUProfiler`.

### Check List

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- [x] Unit test
- [x] Integration test


Side effects

- [ ] Performance regression: Consumes more CPU
- [ ] Performance regression: Consumes more Memory

Documentation

N/A

### Release note

<!-- bugfix or new feature needs a release note -->

```release-note
*: fix bug of profiling conflict between TopSQL and pprof profile HTTP API
```

issue_context.title: Continuous Profiling do cpu profile maybe conflict with TopSQL
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

Since both `Continuous Profiling` and `TopSQL` need to do cpu profiling. there are conflict exist since golang only allow 1 profiling by `pprof.StartCPUProfile` at one time.

<!-- a step by step guide for reproducing the bug. -->

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)
To avoid conflict.

### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)

<!-- Paste the output of SELECT tidb_version() -->

```
master:
92207005ec8e37b545d810ec35da477844cca2f4 
```
comments: Please check whether the issue should be labeled with 'affects-x.y' or 'fixes-x.y.z', and then remove 'needs-more-info' label.

review_comments: The name is misleading that people may think that CPU profiling is started, but actually it is not. Could you find some better name? How about something like StartTicker and StopTicker?
em... the name is `StartCPUProfiler`, not `StartCPUProfiling`, Is this also misleading?

Of course, what does a CPU Profiler do? A CPU Profiler do profiling. So starting a CPU Profiler is starting CPU profiling, unless other people have looked at your implementation -- this already indicates that the name is bad, as the name is a part of the public API, where the quality of the API has nothing related with your implementation.
How about rename to `StartCPUProfileController?

Maybe you will find your unit testing easier if it is not a "global", but a "default". The `package.DefaultXxx` pattern is widely used to make the API easy to use while maintaining testability, as for something `Default`, there is still possibility to be not a default, which makes it fully testable.
What about other collectors? Do they need to be closed?
There are no other collectors in `RemoteTopSQLReporter`.
What will happen if I call twice?
Got
The second call will get an error.
How about use a init() to assign the `globalTopSQLReport`? Then you don't need to worry about it is possibly nil. You can start its internal goroutine later in `SetupTopSQL`.
done.
I'm not sure, but maybe both `data.Begin` and `data.End` doesn't need to exist? Seems that nobody actually cares them.
great, already removed.
Why not simply keep `globalTopSQLReport` in type `reporter.RemoteTopSQLReporter`? Then you don't need a type check any more.
`globalTopSQLReport` use `reporter.TopSQLReporter` is for the test, since some the use the `mock.TopSQLCollector`
Seems that when address is empty at that time, register will not be called. Will register be called later when address becomes not empty?
Yes, it will be called later in `trySwitchRegistration`.
addressed, PTAL again.
There is a double wait here (the previous wait is at L119). Will this cause deadlocks?
yes, already fix me.
"Loop" is duplicated with "Cycle". They are same meanings. Please change names to clearly indicate their different roles.

how about simply allocating a fixed size buffer by default? For now you are updating the `lastDataSize` for each time, but the size may vary, sometimes big and sometimes small. I'm afraid this might not be able to avoid all re-allocations.
I'm not sure whether a sync pool is a better choice if you really like to reduce allocations here.

The problem is, the profile data size may vary in different kinds of loads, so It is hard to find a suitable `fixed size`.

But if the loads are same, then the profile data size of each second should also similar. And we can assume the load per second is similar to the previous second.

How about aligning with 4KB boundaries? e.g. always to be (4 * N) KB. In this way, small workload varies will still be suitable while also possible to adjust dynamically when the workload changes drastically.
ok
The name is misleading. A `doXxx` function in Golang usually means it does something and waits for it. But this function is not. Please either change your API name or change or implementation.
Please reduce your L82 to L243 to within 50 LOC. You made a simple thing really unnecessarily complex.
Seems that usually this package is referenced as `topsqlstate`, so that this can be named as `Enabled`?
How about do this refactor in another PR, since this PR already very large.
